beforeRecord.q: An economy has 90 employed, 10 unemployed, and 50 not in the labor force. Five employed workers lose jobs and search; five unemployed workers stop searching. What happens to unemployment rate?
options: It rises slightly to 10.5%
It rises to 15%
It falls to 5%
It becomes 0%
beforeRecord.feedback: Employed falls to 85. Five newly unemployed workers replace five workers who stop searching, so unemployed remains 10 and the labor force falls to 95. The rate is 10/95 = 10.53%. The unchanged unemployed count does not imply an unchanged unemployment rate: employment and the labor-force denominator have both fallen.
